\chapter{Complexity — Oblivious Setup}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Robustness.ObliviousSetup
\section{Overview}

This module analyses the initialization (setup) phase of the length-only oblivious
schedule machine attached to a Turing machine $W$ over the Boolean alphabet and a
padding parameter $a$.  The explicit configuration \lean{Complexity.setupCfg} isolates
the machine's three controller tapes --- the binary budget tape, the unary macrostep
counter, and the sweep guide --- and phase-by-phase run identities give the exact cost
of the input reset, the copy of the input onto the guide, the fixed-width
binary-to-unary budget conversion, and the two-sided guide-zone allocation.  They
compose into \lean{Complexity.setupCfg_initializes}, the complete initialization run
with its exact duration.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Explicit setup configuration]
\lean{Complexity.setupCfg}
\label{Complexity.setupCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.OblPhase, Complexity.OblSymbol, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM}
Let $W$ be a Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with $k$ work tapes and let
$a \in \bbn$ be a padding parameter; the oblivious schedule machine built from $W$ and
$a$ has $k+3$ work tapes over the schedule alphabet.  Given an input word $x$ of
schedule symbols, a base configuration $c$ on $x$, a controller phase $q$ (possibly the
halting state), an input-head position $p \in \{0,\dots,|x|+1\}$, integers
$b, u, g \in \bbz$, and tape contents $\beta, \mu, \gamma \colon \bbz \to
\Sigma \cup \{\text{blank}\}$ (where $\Sigma$ is the schedule alphabet), the associated
setup configuration is the configuration with state $q$ and input head at $p$, whose
first $k$ work tapes and head positions agree with those of $c$, whose last three
(controller) tapes --- the binary budget, unary macrostep counter, and sweep guide ---
have contents $\beta, \mu, \gamma$ with heads at $b, u, g$ respectively, and whose
output agrees with that of $c$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Optional write on one tape]
\lean{Complexity.setupWrite}
\label{Complexity.setupWrite}
\leanok
Given a tape $t \colon \bbz \to A \cup \{\text{blank}\}$, a cell $z \in \bbz$, and an
optional write instruction, the resulting tape is $t$ itself when no write is
requested, and otherwise $t$ updated at cell $z$ with the requested (possibly blank)
symbol.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Action on a setup configuration]
\lean{Complexity.setupCfg_apply}
\label{Complexity.setupCfg_apply}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.OblPhase, Complexity.OblSymbol, Complexity.finThree_cases, Complexity.oblAction, Complexity.setupCfg, Complexity.setupWrite, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.moveInputPos}
\difficulty{4}
Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with $k$ work tapes, let
$a\in\mathbb{N}$, and fix an input word $x$ over the schedule alphabet. Given a base
configuration $c$ on $x$, phases $q,q'$, an input-head position
$p\in\{0,\ldots,|x|+1\}$, head positions $b,u,g\in\mathbb{Z}$, and tape contents
$\beta,\mu,\gamma\colon\mathbb{Z}\to\mathrm{Option}(\text{schedule alphabet})$, apply an
action with next phase $q'$, input-head move $d\in\{-1,0,+1\}$, and write–move
instructions $(w_b,m_b),(w_u,m_u),(w_g,m_g)$ on the three controller tapes. The result
is the setup configuration with phase $q'$, input-head position obtained by moving $p$
by $d$ with clamping to $\{0,\ldots,|x|+1\}$, controller heads at $b+m_b,u+m_u,g+m_g$,
and controller tapes updated at their respective old head positions according to the
optional writes; its first $k$ work tapes, their head positions, and its output agree
with $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Input symbol in a setup configuration]
\lean{Complexity.setupCfg_input}
\label{Complexity.setupCfg_input}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.OblPhase, Complexity.OblSymbol, Complexity.setupCfg, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.FinTM}
\difficulty{2}
Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $a\in\mathbb{N}$, let
$x$ be a word of schedule symbols, and choose a base configuration on $x$, a controller
phase, a valid input-head position $p$, three integer head positions, and three
controller tapes. In the resulting setup configuration, the input symbol read is blank
if $p=0$; otherwise it is the symbol of $x$ at zero-based index $p-1$, or blank if that
index is outside $x$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Partially copied guide tape]
\lean{Complexity.copyGuide}
\label{Complexity.copyGuide}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.OblSymbol}
For $j \in \bbn$, the partial guide after copying $j$ input cells is the tape whose
cell $-1$ carries an interior mark (the virtual left boundary), whose cells $z$ with
$0 \le z < j$ carry the origin mark at $z = 0$ and interior marks otherwise, and whose
remaining cells are blank.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Extending the Partial Copy Guide]
\lean{Complexity.copyGuide_next}
\label{Complexity.copyGuide_next}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.copyGuide}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $j$, updating the partial copy guide at coordinate $j$ with the
origin mark if $j=0$ and the interior mark otherwise yields the partial copy guide for
$j+1$ copied input cells.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Uniqueness of the Guide Origin]
\lean{Complexity.copyGuide_origin}
\label{Complexity.copyGuide_origin}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.copyGuide}
\difficulty{2}
For every natural number $j>0$ and every integer coordinate $z$, the partial copy guide
after $j$ cells has the origin mark at $z$ if and only if $z=0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Copy loop phase]
\lean{Complexity.copyPhase}
\label{Complexity.copyPhase}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.OblPhase}
The controller phase of the copy loop after $j$ copied symbols: the first-copy phase

otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Cost and outcome of a budget round]

\difficulty{4}
Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over Boolean symbols, let $a,N\in\mathbb{N}$, and let
$x$ be a finite schedule-alphabet word. Given any base configuration on $x$, input-head
position, integer guide-head coordinate $g$, Boolean word $w$, and guide tape, start the
length-only schedule in budget-start phase with the budget head at $|w|+1$ over the
captured clock tape for $w$, and the unary head at $N+1$ over the unary tape with $N$
markers. After exactly $2|w|+(a+1)+4$ steps, the budget tape contains the result of a
borrow pass with incoming borrow set on $w$, the unary tape has $N+a+1$ markers and its
head is at $N+(a+1)+1$, the budget head is at $|w|+1$, and the phase is unary-start if
the borrow pass ends with a borrow and budget-start otherwise; the input head, base
data, guide tape and guide head are unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Complete Binary-to-Unary Conversion]
\lean{Complexity.setupCfg_budget_all}
\label{Complexity.setupCfg_budget_all}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.OblPhase, Complexity.OblSymbol, Complexity.budgetBorrow, Complexity.budgetBorrow_length, Complexity.budgetBorrow_underflow, Complexity.budgetBorrow_value, Complexity.budgetValue, Complexity.clockTape, Complexity.obliviousSchedule, Complexity.setupCfg, Complexity.setupCfg_budget_round, Complexity.unaryTape, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add}
\difficulty{5}
Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over Boolean symbols, let $a,N,v\in\mathbb{N}$, and
let $x$ be a finite word over the schedule alphabet. Choose a base configuration on
input $x$, an input-head position $p$, an integer guide-head position $g$, and
guide-tape contents $\gamma\colon\mathbb{Z}\to\mathrm{Option}(\mathrm{OblSymbol})$. For
every bit word $w$ of little-endian value $v$, running the length-only schedule machine
from the setup configuration in the budget-start phase, with budget head at $|w|+1$ on
the captured clock tape of $w$ and unary head at $N+1$ on the unary tape with $N$
markers, for exactly $(v+1)(2|w|+(a+1)+4)$ steps yields the setup configuration in the
unary-start phase with the same base configuration, input-head position, and guide tape
and head, with budget head still at $|w|+1$ and unary head at $N+(a+1)(v+1)+1$. Its
budget tape is the captured clock tape of some bit word $w'$ with $|w'|=|w|$, and its
unary tape has $N+(a+1)(v+1)$ markers.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Uniqueness of the origin marker]
\lean{Complexity.unaryTape_origin}
\label{Complexity.unaryTape_origin}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.unaryTape}
\difficulty{2}
For every $N\in\mathbb{N}$ and every integer cell position $z$, the unary tape with $N$
markers carries the origin marker at $z$ if and only if $z=0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Unit markers on the unary tape]
\lean{Complexity.unaryTape_unit}

\leanok
\uses{Complexity.unaryTape}
\difficulty{1}
For every $N,j\in\mathbb{N}$ with $j<N$, the unary tape with $N$ markers carries a unit
marker at cell $j+1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[End of the unary tape]
\lean{Complexity.unaryTape_end}
\label{Complexity.unaryTape_end}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.unaryTape}
\difficulty{1}
For every $N\in\mathbb{N}$, the unary tape with $N$ markers is blank at cell $N+1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Common phase of the two unary rewinds]
\lean{Complexity.unaryRewindPhase}
\label{Complexity.unaryRewindPhase}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.OblPhase}
The controller phase used to rewind the unary counter: the unary-reset phase when the
Boolean flag marks the final rewind, and the unary-back phase otherwise.  Both rewinds
follow the same path and differ only in their successor phase.
\end{definition}

let $last\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. For any input word, base configuration,
input-head position, budget-head position and tape, and guide-head position and tape,
starting in the unary-rewind phase (unary-reset if $last$ is true and unary-back
otherwise) with unary head at $j$ and unary tape containing $N$ markers, after $j+1$
steps the unary head is at $1$ and the phase is start-center if $last$ is true and the
first rightward layout phase otherwise; the resulting configuration has all the same
data and other head positions.

Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet and let $a,N\in\bbn$. For
any input word, base configuration, input-head position, budget-head position and tape,

\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Interior guide mark]
\lean{Complexity.guideMark}
\label{Complexity.guideMark}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.OblSymbol}
The symbol written to guide cell $z$ during allocation: the origin mark when $z = 0$
and an interior mark otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Partially allocated guide tape]
\lean{Complexity.guideFill}
\label{Complexity.guideFill}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.OblSymbol, Complexity.guideMark}
Given a direction (rightward or leftward), a guide tape $\gamma$, and $j \in \bbn$, the
$j$-cell filled version of $\gamma$ is the tape agreeing with $\gamma$ except that each
cell $z$ with $0 \le z < j$ (rightward) respectively $0 \le -z < j$ (leftward) is
overwritten with the guide mark of $z$: the origin mark at $0$ and interior marks
elsewhere, independently of the previous contents.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Empty allocation prefix]
\lean{Complexity.guideFill_zero}
\label{Complexity.guideFill_zero}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.OblSymbol, Complexity.guideFill}
\difficulty{2}
For either direction of filling and any guide tape on the integer coordinates, filling
zero cells leaves the tape unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Origin preservation under allocation]
\lean{Complexity.guideFill_origin}
\label{Complexity.guideFill_origin}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.OblSymbol, Complexity.guideFill, Complexity.guideMark}
\difficulty{2}
Let $ho$ be either direction, and let $\\gamma$ be a guide tape whose origin mark
occurs exactly at coordinate $0$. For every natural number $j$ and every integer
coordinate $z$, the $j$-cell filled tape carries the origin mark at $z$ if and only if
$z=0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[One more allocated cell]
\lean{Complexity.guideFill_next}
\label{Complexity.guideFill_next}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.OblSymbol, Complexity.guideFill, Complexity.guideMark}
\difficulty{4}
Let $ho$ be either the rightward or leftward direction, let $\\gamma$ be a guide tape,
and let $j$ be a natural number. Updating the $j$-cell filled tape at coordinate $j$ in
the rightward direction or $-j$ in the leftward direction with the guide mark for that
coordinate yields the $(j+1)$-cell filled tape.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Phases of the outward allocation passes]
\lean{Complexity.layoutPhase}
\label{Complexity.layoutPhase}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.OblPhase}
The finite controller phase of an outward allocation pass, indexed by
$i \in \{0,1,2\}$: the rightward layout phases when the direction flag is set and the
leftward layout phases otherwise.  The two passes are symmetric.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Allocation head movement]
\lean{Complexity.layoutMove}
\label{Complexity.layoutMove}
\leanok
The guide-head movement of an allocation pass: one cell to the right for the rightward
pass and one cell to the left for the leftward pass, independently of the cell
contents.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[One allocation step]
\lean{Complexity.setupCfg_layout_step}

Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $a\in\mathbb{N}$, and
consider a setup configuration with arbitrary base configuration, input-head position,
integer controller-head positions, and controller tapes. Suppose its phase is the
allocation phase of direction $r\in\{\mathrm{right},\mathrm{left}\}$ indexed by
$i\in\{0,1,2\}$, the unary tape reads a unit marker at its head, and the guide tape
reads the origin marker at its head if and only if that head is at cell $0$. One step
advances the allocation index to $i+1\pmod 3$, moves the unary head right by one exactly
when $i=2$, moves the guide head one cell in direction $r$, and writes the origin marker
at the guide cell previously under its head if that cell is $0$, writing an interior
marker otherwise; all other tape contents and configuration data are unchanged.
\end{lemma}

and choose a direction. Assume the unary tape has a unit marker at $u$ and the guide
tape carries the origin mark exactly at coordinate $0$. From allocation index $i$ with
guide head at $j$ in the rightward direction or $-j$ in the leftward direction, and with
the guide tape filled through $j$ cells in that direction, one step advances the
allocation index cyclically, advances the unary head by one exactly when $i=2$, moves
the guide head one cell in the chosen direction, and leaves the guide filled through
$j+1$ cells.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Successor modulo three]
\lean{Complexity.nextThird_mod}
\label{Complexity.nextThird_mod}

and choose a schedule-symbol input, a base configuration, a valid input-head position,
an integer budget-head position, and tapes $\beta,\gamma$. Assume $j\le 3B$ and that
$\gamma$ carries the origin mark exactly at coordinate $0$. After $j$ steps from
allocation index $0$, with unary head at $1$ over the unary tape with $B$ markers and
guide head at $0$, the allocation index is $j$ modulo $3$, the unary head is at $\lfloor

leftward direction; the guide tape is the result of filling $j$ cells of $\gamma$ in
that direction.

\begin{lemma}[End of an outward allocation pass]

Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $a,B\in\mathbb{N}$,
and choose a schedule-symbol input, a base configuration on it, a valid input-head

head position $g$.

\begin{lemma}[Origin marker on the right guide]
\lean{Complexity.rightGuide_origin}

\difficulty{5}
Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet with $k$ work tapes, let $a
\in \mathbb{N}$, and let $x$ be a finite word over the schedule alphabet. For any base
configuration on $x$, input-head position $p$, integer budget-head position $b$, and
budget tape contents $\beta$, let $n,B \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $n+1 \le B$. Starting
from the setup configuration in the unary-start phase with unary head at $B+1$ over the
unary tape with $B$ markers, unary head contents as specified by that tape, and guide
head at $0$ over the partial guide with $n+1$ copied cells, after exactly $14B+10$ steps
the machine is in the macrostep-check phase, with unary head at $1$ over the same unary
tape and guide head at $0$ over the guide of radius $3B$; the clock tapes, budget tape
and head, input-head position, and output are unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{4}
Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over Boolean symbols, let $a\in\mathbb{N}$, and let
$x$ be a finite schedule-alphabet word. For any base configuration on $x$, integers
$b,u$, and budget and unary tapes, starting in copy-left phase with input head at
position $1$, guide head at cell $0$, and blank guide tape, after exactly $2|x|+4$ steps
the machine is in budget-start phase with input head at position $|x|+1$, guide head at
cell $0$, and guide tape equal to the partial guide with $|x|+1$ copied cells; the base
data, budget tape and head, unary tape and head are unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{4}
Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $a\in\mathbb{N}$, and
let $x$ be a Boolean input. For any configuration $c$ of $W$ on $x$ whose state is
absent, the clock-stage configuration of $c$ equals the setup configuration based on
that clock-stage configuration, with control phase reset-start and the same input-head
position. Its binary budget tape has the captured clock tape of the output word of $c$
and head at $|c.output|+1$; its unary counter has only the origin marker and head at
$1$; and its guide tape is blank with head at $0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Macrostep Retargeting of a Setup Configuration]
\lean{Complexity.macroCfg_setup}
\label{Complexity.macroCfg_setup}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.OblPhase, Complexity.OblSymbol, Complexity.finThree_cases, Complexity.macroCfg, Complexity.setupCfg, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM}
\difficulty{3}
Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $a$ be a natural
number, let $x$ be a word over the schedule alphabet, and let $c$ be a configuration
with $k+3$ work tapes on input $x$. For optional phases $q,q'$, an input-head position
$p$, integers $b,u,g,u',g'$, and tape-content functions $\beta,\mu,\gamma : \mathbb{Z}
\to \text{Option}(\text{schedule alphabet})$, first form the setup configuration from
$c$ with phase $q$, input-head position $p$, tape heads at $b,u,g$, and contents
$\beta,\mu,\gamma$ on the last three tapes. Applying the macrostep construction to this
configuration with phase $q'$ and unary-counter and guide head positions $u',g'$ gives
exactly the setup configuration based on $c$ with phase $q'$, input-head position $p$,
tape heads at $b,u',g'$, and the same tape contents and output.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Completion of the macrostep schedule]
\lean{Complexity.setupCfg_finish}
\label{Complexity.setupCfg_finish}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.OblPhase, Complexity.OblSymbol, Complexity.guideTape, Complexity.macroCfg_finish, Complexity.macroCfg_setup, Complexity.obliviousSchedule, Complexity.setupCfg, Complexity.unaryTape, Complexity.unaryTape_end, Complexity.unaryTape_unit, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom}
\difficulty{3}
Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $a,B\in\mathbb{N}$,
and let $x$ be a word of schedule symbols. Choose a base configuration on $x$, an
input-head position $p$, an integer $b$, and a binary-budget tape $\beta$. Starting in
the macrostep-check phase with unary head at $1$, unary tape containing $B$ markers, and
guide head at $0$ over the guide of radius $3B$, after exactly $B(6(3B)+8)+1$ steps the
machine is halted, with unary head at $B+1$; the input head, budget head and tape, unary
tape, guide head and tape, and all clock tapes and output are otherwise as specified by
the same setup configuration.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Initialization of the schedule configuration]
\lean{Complexity.setupCfg_initializes}
\label{Complexity.setupCfg_initializes}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.OblPhase, Complexity.OblSymbol, Complexity.budgetValue, Complexity.clockTape, Complexity.copyGuide, Complexity.guideTape, Complexity.obliviousSchedule, Complexity.setupCfg, Complexity.setupCfg_allocation, Complexity.setupCfg_budget_all, Complexity.setupCfg_copy, Complexity.setupCfg_reset, Complexity.unaryTape, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add}
\difficulty{4}
Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $a,v\in\mathbb{N}$,
let $x$ be a word of schedule symbols, and choose a base configuration on $x$, a valid
input-head position $p$, and a bit word $w$ whose little-endian value is $v$. Assume
$|x|+1\le (a+1)(v+1)$. Then there is a bit word $w'$ of the same length as $w$ such
that, after exactly $(p-1+2)+(2|x|+4)+(v+1)(2|w|+(a+1)+4)+14(a+1)(v+1)+10$ steps from
the reset-start setup with budget head at $|w|+1$, unary head at $1$ over the empty
unary counter, and blank guide, the machine is in the macrostep-check phase with input
head at $|x|+1$, budget head at $|w|+1$ over the captured clock tape for $w'$, unary
head at $1$ over the unary tape with $(a+1)(v+1)$ markers, and guide head at $0$ over
the guide of radius $3(a+1)(v+1)$.
\end{lemma}
